profile.summary: DNABERT is a DNA language model that applies the BERT approach from natural language processing to genomic DNA. It reads a DNA sequence of up to 512 tokens, split into k-mers, and is pretrained on the human genome by predicting masked k-mers. Users fine-tune it with a small labelled data set to predict features such as promoters, splice sites and transcription factor binding sites, and can inspect its attention to find motifs and score variants.

summary_quotes.text: DNABERT takes a sequence with a max length of 512 as input.
we tokenized it into a sequence of k-mers
on prediction of promoters, splice sites and transcription factor binding sites, after easy fine-tuning using small task-specific labeled data

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: DNABERT adapts the BERT language model to DNA. A sequence is cut into k-mers, each base joined with the bases that follow it, and these k-mers become the tokens. During pretraining on human genome sequences, the model sees contiguous spans of k-mers masked (about 15% of the input, raised to 20% for the last 20k of 120k steps) and learns to predict them, so it learns general patterns of DNA from unlabelled data. The pretrained model is then fine-tuned with a small labelled data set for a specific task. The repository adds tools to visualise attention, find motifs and score the effect of sequence variants with a fine-tuned model.

quotes.text: we tokenized it into a sequence of k-mers
by concatenating it with its following ones
considering a token could be trivially inferred from the immediately surrounding k-mers (total ∼15% of input sequence)
We pre-trained DNABERT for 120k steps with a batch size of 2000.
In the last 20k steps, we increased the masking rate to 20 percent.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There are four pretrained checkpoints, one for each k-mer size from 3 to 6, with the same architecture and settings. The paper reports results with k = 6 because it performed best, and says k = 3 to 6 gave very similar results. The README's download links have expired and point users to the Hugging Face copies. A result should name the k-mer size and the Hugging Face revision; this page read DNA_bert_6 at revision c56e67ea. The repository extends code from Hugging Face transformers and its README sets up a Python 3.6 environment with CUDA 10.0, and the README recommends checking out DNABERT-2 for newer work.

quotes.text: In all experiments, we report results of kmer = 6 since it achieves the best performance.
The original links to the pretrained DNABERT models (DNABERT-3, 4, 5, 6) have expired.
Please check out DNABERT-2 if you are interested in our work.
We extended codes from [huggingface](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers) and adapted them to the DNA scenario.
conda install pytorch torchvision cudatoolkit=10.0 -c pytorch

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Pretrained DNA language model (BERT-style bidirectional encoder) that is fine-tuned for sequence-level and token-level prediction tasks.

quotes.text: we developed a novel pre-trained bidirectional encoder representation, named DNABERT
The pre-trained DNABERT model can be fine-tuned with task-specific training data for applications in various sequence- and token-level prediction tasks.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Same architecture as BERT base: 12 transformer layers with 768 hidden units and 12 attention heads. Pretraining drops BERT's next-sentence prediction and masks contiguous spans of k tokens.

quotes.text: which consists of 12 Transformer layers with 768 hidden units and 12 attention heads in each layer
removing next sentence prediction, adjusting the sequence length and forcing the model to predict contiguous k tokens adapting to DNA scenario

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA sequences tokenised into k-mers (k = 3, 4, 5 or 6; for example ATGGCT becomes the 3-mers ATG, TGG, GGC, GCT), with [CLS] and [SEP] tokens added; the repository scripts expect sequences already converted to k-mer format.

quotes.text: we tokenized it into a sequence of k-mers and added a special token [CLS] at the beginning of it
a DNA sequence ‘ATGGCT’ can be tokenized to a sequence of four 3-mers: {ATG, TGG, GGC, GCT}
we respectively set k as 3,4,5 and 6 and train 4 different models
Note that the sequences are in kmer format, so you will need to convert your sequences into that.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: From the pretrained model, masked k-mer predictions and token representations. After fine-tuning, task predictions (for example promoter, splice site or transcription factor binding site classification), attention scores for visualisation and motif analysis, and mutation effect scores.

quotes.text: on prediction of promoters, splice sites and transcription factor binding sites
Visualiazation of DNABERT consists of 2 steps.
as well as the difference score and log odds ratio of the change in every case

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not stated as a count in the sources read. The four models share the BERT base architecture (12 layers, 768 hidden units, 12 heads); vocabulary size differs with k (4,101 tokens in the DNA_bert_6 config).

quotes.text: the same parameter setting across all the four DNABERT models during pre-training

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Human genome sequences, generated by non-overlapping splitting and random sampling, 5 to 510 long according to Methods 2.2.2 (Section 2.1 says 10 to 510); the paper does not explain the difference. The sources read do not name the genome assembly.

quotes.text: We generated training data from human genome via two approaches: direct non-overlap splitting and random sampling, with length of the sequence between 5 and 510.
based on 10 to 510-length sequences extracted from human genome via truncation and sampling

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: Four pretrained models, DNABERT-3, DNABERT-4, DNABERT-5 and DNABERT-6, one per k-mer size, now on Hugging Face as zhihan1996/DNA_bert_3 to DNA_bert_6. The README also offers a DNABERT-6 model fine-tuned on its sample data. DNABERT-2 is a separate, later model.

quotes.text: We also provide a model with `KMER=6` that is fine-tuned on the sample dataset
The second generation of DNABERT, named [DNABERT-2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.15006), is publically available at https://github.com/Zhihan1996/DNABERT_2.

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not reported. The paper does not date the genome data or the training run in the passages read.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 512 tokens, including [CLS] and [SEP]. The paper splits longer sequences into pieces and concatenates their representations (DNABERT-XL).

quotes.text: DNABERT takes a sequence with a max length of 512 as input.
For sequences longer than 512, we split them into pieces and concatenate their representations as the final representation.

facts.label: Weights licence
facts.value: Not stated for the weights. The Hugging Face card metadata of the four checkpoints has no licence field. The repository's Apache-2.0 LICENSE does not mention the weights.

facts.label: Code licence
facts.value: Apache-2.0 (Apache License, Version 2.0), from the repository LICENSE file.

strengths.text: Code is Apache-2.0 and the repository covers the full cycle: pretraining, fine-tuning, prediction, attention visualisation, motif finding and variant scoring.
The authors report that a model pretrained on the human genome can be applied to other organisms after fine-tuning.

quotes.text: Finally, we demonstrate that pre-trained DNABERT with human genome can even be readily applied to other organisms with exceptional performance.

strengths.text: Four k-mer sizes are released, so users can choose the tokenisation; the authors found little difference between them.

quotes.text: DNABERT with k = 3, 4, 5, 6 achieved very similar performances with slight fluctuations.

limitations.text: Input is limited to 512 tokens; longer sequences must be split into pieces.

quotes.text: DNABERT takes a sequence with a max length of 512 as input.
For sequences longer than 512, we split them into pieces

limitations.text: Trained on the human genome only; the sources read describe no multi-species pretraining. The authors point to DNABERT-2, trained on multi-species genomes, as the successor.

quotes.text: We generated training data from human genome
DNABERT-2 is trained on multi-species genomes and is more efficient, powerful, and easy to use than its first generation.

limitations.text: The software stack is old: the README environment uses Python 3.6, CUDA 10.0 and an NVIDIA GPU, and the original model download links have expired.

run_guide.summary: Set up the repository environment, then fine-tune the pretrained DNABERT-6 model on the repository's sample promoter data and make predictions.
prerequisites: Linux with at least one NVIDIA GPU and driver version 410.48 or later (CUDA 10.0), and Anaconda, as the README states. The authors trained on 8 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti GPUs with 11 GB memory.
The pretrained DNABERT-6 files from https://huggingface.co/zhihan1996/DNA_bert_6 downloaded into a local directory. The README gives no download command.
Code is Apache-2.0. No licence is stated for the weights.

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
conda create -n dnabert python=3.6
conda activate dnabert
steps.explanation: Creates and activates the Python 3.6 conda environment the README recommends.

steps.title: Install the package at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
conda install pytorch torchvision cudatoolkit=10.0 -c pytorch

git clone https://github.com/jerryji1993/DNABERT
cd DNABERT
git checkout --detach b6da04ec9a7d4e53efe5b33a6ce1a21c0e7ac413
python3 -m pip install --editable .
cd examples
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
steps.explanation: The README's install commands, with a checkout line added to pin the commit this page read.

quotes.text: conda install pytorch torchvision cudatoolkit=10.0 -c pytorch

steps.title: Fine-tune DNABERT-6 on the sample data
steps.shell:
export KMER=6
export MODEL_PATH=PATH_TO_THE_PRETRAINED_MODEL
export DATA_PATH=sample_data/ft/$KMER
export OUTPUT_PATH=./ft/$KMER

python run_finetune.py \
    --model_type dna \
    --tokenizer_name=dna$KMER \
    --model_name_or_path $MODEL_PATH \
    --task_name dnaprom \
    --do_train \
    --do_eval \
    --data_dir $DATA_PATH \
    --max_seq_length 100 \
    --per_gpu_eval_batch_size=32   \
    --per_gpu_train_batch_size=32   \
    --learning_rate 2e-4 \
    --num_train_epochs 5.0 \
    --output_dir $OUTPUT_PATH \
    --evaluate_during_training \
    --logging_steps 100 \
    --save_steps 4000 \
    --warmup_percent 0.1 \
    --hidden_dropout_prob 0.1 \
    --overwrite_output \
    --weight_decay 0.01 \
    --n_process 8
steps.explanation: The README's fine-tuning example, run from the examples directory. Replace PATH_TO_THE_PRETRAINED_MODEL with the directory holding the downloaded DNABERT-6 files.

steps.title: Predict with the fine-tuned model
steps.shell:
export KMER=6
export MODEL_PATH=./ft/$KMER
export DATA_PATH=sample_data/ft/$KMER
export PREDICTION_PATH=./result/$KMER

python run_finetune.py \
    --model_type dna \
    --tokenizer_name=dna$KMER \
    --model_name_or_path $MODEL_PATH \
    --task_name dnaprom \
    --do_predict \
    --data_dir $DATA_PATH  \
    --max_seq_length 75 \
    --per_gpu_pred_batch_size=128   \
    --output_dir $MODEL_PATH \
    --predict_dir $PREDICTION_PATH \
    --n_process 48
steps.explanation: The README's prediction example. It loads the fine-tuned model from ./ft/6 and predicts on dev.tsv in the sample data.

outputs: A fine-tuned model in ./ft/6, and prediction results for the sample dev.tsv saved under ./result/6, as the README describes.
